title: Briefing: Water Utility Ransomware Incident
confidence_notes: Speaker notes assume a 20-minute internal briefing slot.

slides.title: Ransomware at a Regional Water Utility
slides.speaker_notes: Set expectations: this is a corporate-network incident with public-service consequences, not an attack on control systems.

slides.title: What Happened
bullets: Eleven servers encrypted, including billing and historian
slides.speaker_notes: Emphasise the detection-to-containment time and that the operational impact was limited by design.

slides.title: How They Got In
slides.speaker_notes: This is the single most important slide. Every remediation flows from the identity failure.

slides.title: Impact and Recovery
bullets: Offline backups at separate site intact
slides.speaker_notes: Contrast the two backup outcomes to motivate the backup-isolation recommendation.

slides.title: What We Are Changing
bullets: Rotate all contractor credentials, enforce MFA
Isolate backup infrastructure from domain admins
Deploy EDR to servers and engineering workstations
slides.speaker_notes: Give each item an owner and a date when presenting live.

slides.title: Takeaway
bullets: Identity hygiene is the weak point
slides.speaker_notes: Close on the positive: the design worked. Then pivot to the identity work that still needs funding.

deck_summary: A six-slide internal briefing on the September 2024 ransomware intrusion, its limited operational impact, and the four remediation workstreams now underway.
